codes.title: paths this kit may not touch stand where it must install
codes.explanation: Adoption found paths in a governed plane that no reading explains, and the kit has no permission to take them over. Every such path is named, and the operation stops rather than the path being overwritten. Give each named path a class (or move it), then run again.

codes.title: a readable declaration is absent, unreadable, invalid, or claims one identity twice
codes.explanation: A collection the kit reads could not be read honestly: a member is missing, is not valid for its schema, or two members claim the same identity. A collection with two answers for one identity has no answer. Repair or remove the named member.

codes.title: an instance and its base both carry one key
codes.explanation: A composed declaration and the base it extends both set the same key. The kit refuses rather than choosing a winner, because the losing side would go on declaring a value the composition does not have. Remove the key from one side.

codes.title: a host truth is absent, unreadable, or does not honour its schema
codes.explanation: A binding the host owns (under its project plane) could not be read as the schema declares it. The kit will not act on a host it cannot measure. Restore or correct the named binding.

codes.title: a declared source of rules is missing, or a name resolves to two things
codes.explanation: A declaration names a source of rules that does not exist, or a name reaches two sources. Rules read from an ambiguous source would be obeyed by whichever was found first. Declare the source once.

codes.title: no plane, or more than one, is declared for observed state
codes.explanation: Observed (ephemeral) state needs exactly one declared plane to live in. None means it has nowhere to go; two means a name resolves to two places. Declare exactly one ephemeral plane in the manifest.

codes.title: the install is drafted and waits at the human door
codes.explanation: Not a failure: a declared state. The host was measured, a set was resolved and an answer drafted, and the one human approval in the design has not been given. Review the draft and run again with --approve <who>. Exits 3 so a stalled install is never mistaken for a broken one.

codes.title: the host's record of what it received is absent or cannot be honestly taken
codes.explanation: The estate -- the host's record of what the kit delivered -- is missing or unreadable, so no reconciliation against it can be trusted. Restore the estate record, or adopt the host afresh.

codes.title: a residence rule carries a pattern that is not a pattern
codes.explanation: A hygiene residence rule declares a path pattern that cannot be compiled. A rule that matches nothing reports a clean host that was never measured. Correct the named pattern.

codes.title: a host lock document exists and cannot be read as one
codes.explanation: The host's lock (the hold a running verb takes) is present but unreadable. It is refused rather than overwritten, because a hold nobody can read may still have somebody standing behind it. Confirm nothing is running, then release it with --break-lock <who>.

codes.title: a card, a move or a board contradicts the declared lifecycle
codes.explanation: Work cards move only along the transitions the lifecycle declares. The named card, move or board breaks that declaration. Move the card along a declared transition, or change the lifecycle declaration.

codes.title: the kit cannot state what it is made of
codes.explanation: Building the kit's own lock found a rule that measures nothing, a directory account with no suffix, or one path accounted for twice. A kit that cannot enumerate itself cannot be shipped honestly. Correct the manifest's accounts.

codes.title: an observer kind is unprovided, or claimed by two modules
codes.explanation: A declaration names an observer kind that no discovered module provides, or two modules claim the same kind. A name resolving to two meanings is refused rather than ordered. Provide the kind once.

codes.title: a record was asked for in a readable the capability does not declare
codes.explanation: A receipt was to be written into a readable its capability does not declare. It is refused rather than defaulted: a record written where nobody reads is worse than none, because its absence from the report reads as nothing having happened. Declare the readable, or target a declared one.

codes.title: a payload declaration is missing, unreadable, or does not honour its schema
codes.explanation: The kit's own manifest or one of the declarations it names could not be read as its schema declares. The payload is defective, not the host. Repair the named declaration in the kit.

codes.title: a detector declares an evidence kind the interpreter cannot evaluate
codes.explanation: A detector asked for evidence of a kind no probe knows how to take. A probe that guessed would report a fact nobody measured. Use a declared evidence kind.

codes.title: a path could not be resolved inside the workspace
codes.explanation: A path escapes, or cannot be placed inside, the host workspace. The kit acts only on paths that resolve under the host root. Correct the named path.

codes.title: a write was attempted outside the declared scope
codes.explanation: A verb tried to write a path outside the write set it declared. Refused, never warned about: an undeclared write is how work lands somewhere nobody chose. This is a defect in the declaration that asked for the write.

codes.title: the three readings cannot be reconciled, or one cannot be taken
codes.explanation: Reconciliation compares what the kit ships, what the host received, and what the host holds now. One of the three could not be read honestly, or they contradict in a way no rule resolves. Resolve the named paths.

codes.title: the declared capability set cannot compose
codes.explanation: An unmet provision, a declared conflict, or two capabilities installing to one path. Composition is never resolved by preference; it is refused. Change the selection so every requirement is met exactly once.

codes.title: the host asked for a capability set it may not have
codes.explanation: The selection names a capability nobody declares, or disables one the kit declares structural. Refused before composition, because a selection naming nothing real is a typo the operator must see. Correct --enable / --disable.

codes.title: a template uses syntax outside the supported subset, or names something absent
codes.explanation: A projection template could not be rendered: its syntax is outside the subset the kit supports, or it names a value the view does not carry. Rendering a blank would be a plausible lie. Correct the template.

codes.title: a gate kind is unprovided, or claimed by two modules
codes.explanation: A declaration names a gate kind that no discovered module can evaluate, or two modules claim it. Refused rather than ordered. Provide the kind once.

codes.title: nothing, or more than one capability, declares what to judge
codes.explanation: Evaluation needs exactly one enabled capability declaring what is judged. None leaves nothing to evaluate; two are two homes for one question. Enable exactly one.

codes.title: an install cannot proceed as declared
codes.explanation: A declaration names an install mode the interpreter does not know, the selection contradicts host truth, or a file written does not honour its own schema. Correct the named declaration or selection.

codes.title: the kit no longer matches its own lock
codes.explanation: The kit could not honestly state what it is, or what it is no longer matches kit.lock.json. A kit that differs from its record is not the kit that was reviewed. Re-lock deliberately after review.

codes.title: a move names something the host does not have, or is incomplete
codes.explanation: A card move needs --card, --to and --by, and the card and state must exist in the host. Supply the missing or corrected argument.

codes.title: a projection cannot be rendered without a name meaning two things
codes.explanation: Rendering a projection found two capabilities claiming one view-model name, a record shadowing a view name, or a plural projection whose target, iteration or file naming is not declared soundly. The kit refuses rather than letting one side silently win. Correct the named declaration.

codes.title: an upgrade meets readings that cannot be reconciled
codes.explanation: Upgrading found paths where the shipped, received and held readings contradict. The paths and both moments are named. Resolve each named path, then upgrade again.

codes.title: a gate's stance cannot be honoured as declared
codes.explanation: A stance names no row of the stance vocabulary, a host lowers a gate below the floor its publisher declared, one gate is answered twice, or the kit holds no single stance vocabulary to read. The kit refuses rather than choosing a stance, because a gate standing in a stance nobody declared would report a verdict nobody asked for. Correct the named stance; a floor is lowered only by the gate's publisher, never by a host.

codes.title: an init journal exists and cannot be read as one
codes.explanation: The host's init journal -- the only account of how far an interrupted install got -- is present but unreadable or does not honour the kit's journal schema, or a run was about to write one that does not. It is refused rather than overwritten, because replacing it would destroy the evidence the next run exists to read. Read it, move it aside by hand, then run again.

codes.title: a capability this kit did not issue cannot be taken as it stands
codes.explanation: A capability the kit's own lock does not account for is not the bytes this host pinned when it first took it, is at a version older than the one pinned, or claims a signature its declared verifier refuted -- or the kit holds no single provenance declaration or no lock to tell what it issued. It is refused before any write and no approval opens it: a pin that could be re-taken would pin nothing. Restore the pinned bytes, or have the publisher release a NEWER version, which is met at the door as first contact is.

codes.title: a document was written by a newer kit than this one
codes.explanation: A document the kit was about to read states a schema_version HIGHER than the one this kit's schema for that kind declares. It is refused before its shape is judged, because a shape from the future read through today's schema is a guess, and a guess read as understanding is a surface that lies (ADR-009). Nothing is written. Run the kit version that wrote the document, or upgrade this kit to one that reads its version.

codes.title: a document is at an older version this kit declares no migration for
codes.explanation: A document the kit was about to read states a schema_version LOWER than the one this kit's schema for that kind declares, and this kit ships no migration from that version. It is refused by name rather than read as if it had the current shape (ADR-009). Nothing is written. Run the kit version that wrote the document, or re-create the document with this kit; before 1.0 the kit ships no migrations, and every kind is at version 1.

codes.title: a path cannot change hands as asked
codes.explanation: A host asked to take over a path the kit shipped (ADR-010), and at least one named path cannot be handed over: the host's record does not carry it, it was already taken over (its row names who and when), its steward declares no transfer because the bytes are already the host's or are rebuilt from their inputs, or the transfer names a class this kit does not declare. Every such path is named and none changes hands. Nothing is written. Name only paths the record carries under a steward that offers a transfer.

codes.title: a migration map cannot be read as declared
codes.explanation: A host asked what becomes of its prior agent system (ADR-011), and the migration map it gave -- or the succession vocabulary it is read against -- cannot be read as declared: it is not JSON or not the declared shape, a root or row leaves the host, two rows name one path, a row names a disposition the vocabulary does not declare or omits or adds a field its disposition declares, a reference names no plane or no capability, or two paths are sent to one destination. Every fault is named and no roster is printed. Nothing is written. Correct the map and read again.

codes.title: a succession cannot be carried out as read
codes.explanation: A host asked to carry out its migration map (ADR-012), and the act cannot be carried out whole: no map resides at the declared residence (a map passed from anywhere is refused), the host has no record of what it was given, a path of the prior boundary is still undecided, a row would move or remove a path this kit itself installed or the map itself, a destination already exists, or a destination lies in no space whose mode the succession vocabulary declares may receive a path. Every fault is named and nothing is moved or removed. Answer or correct the map and read again.

codes.title: the accepted roster is not the roster read now
codes.explanation: A succession act was accepted by the digest of its roster, and the roster read at the moment of carrying it out has another digest: the map at its residence or a path of the prior system changed since the reading that was signed, or a path changed while the act was under way, or an interrupted act cannot be reconciled with the tree. Nothing further is moved. Read again with --plan, and sign the digest of what is there now.

codes.title: a path a runtime reads is held by bytes the kit did not write
codes.explanation: A served surface would write a file at a path its runtime product reads -- outside the kit's four planes -- and the file already there matches neither what the kit would render now nor what the kit's own record says it last served there. Those are somebody's bytes, and a projection is rebuilt, never merged, so writing would destroy them. Nothing is written or removed, anywhere. Move the prior file aside, carry a prior agent system over with inherit or takeover (ADR-011, ADR-012), or stop serving the surface; then render again.

codes.title: one path a runtime reads is claimed by two served files
codes.explanation: Two runtimes this host serves -- through one surface or two -- would write the same path, and the kit refuses to decide which one wins: last-writer-wins leaves the loser's declaration reading as delivered. Serve one of them, or declare a surface whose paths do not collide.

codes.title: a kit that is not what it says it is was asked to be pinned or taken as a release
codes.explanation: Delivering the kit into a host (ADR-016) requires a kit that can state what it is: every path accounted for, present and LF. A pinned kit asked to re-deliver ITSELF must still equal the lock it carries -- re-stamping it would launder a change into a fresh reading. A release source (git+<repo>@<rev>#subdirectory=<dir>) must be readable at that revision and its tree must equal its own lock. The paths are named; nothing in the host was written. Fix the kit, or deliver a real release over the pinned copy with upgrade --kit <release>.

codes.title: no capability declares how a DECLARED DIRECTORY is carried by a repository
codes.explanation: A space a capability declares, and a collection projection a host has put nothing into, are directories -- and version control carries files, not directories, so such a path is gone from the next clone and the floor then reports a DRAWN path as missing. The kit writes one marker into every such directory to carry it, and the marker's FILENAME is a declaration: a capability names it in its `space` block, and exactly one capability must -- two would drift, and none would leave the interpreter to invent a name no host was ever told. Declare it in the capability that can never be disabled, so every host is told it.

codes.title: a runtime hook asked to be judged through a surface that declares no hand
codes.explanation: The judge verb (the hook a served runtime setting runs) reads where a product puts the edit it is making -- the edited paths, the introduced text, the exit code that means no -- from that product's surface `hands` declaration. A surface no taken adapter declares, or one without a `hands` block, states none of that, so no edit can be judged and the verb refuses rather than guess. Take the adapter that declares the surface, or declare its `hands`.

codes.title: a capability a host took carries an id the release issued
codes.explanation: A take lives beside the pinned kit and is composed with it by the manifest loader (ADR-018). A take whose id equals one the release issued would shadow the release -- the host would run something no release describes under a name the release owns -- so it is refused by name, at the take and at every load, never resolved by precedence. Remove the take, or take the capability under its own id.

codes.title: a take named no capability that can be taken
codes.explanation: The take verb copies a published capability directory into the host's take plane and records it in the host's take declaration (ADR-018). It refuses a missing --path, a directory with no capability declaration, a declaration that does not honour the capability schema, and a kit that declares no single take plane -- because a take recorded without a capability behind it would be a row describing nothing.

codes.title: a law scope names a directory no served file may be placed in
codes.explanation: A host declares scoped law as a row naming a directory and the law page that binds below it, and every served runtime receives that page at the place it reads nested instructions. The render refuses, before a byte is written, a scope whose directory is not a plain path inside the host, does not exist, is the host root (served by the unscoped briefing), or lies inside a kit plane -- a pinned or taken copy is not the host's to govern, and a file placed there would be governed by nobody who reads it.

codes.title: a setting outside the tree was asked to change that is not the kit's to change, or cannot be measured
codes.explanation: A served surface may declare an activation: a setting in its product's own configuration that must name the served directory before the product runs it. The `activate` door refuses, before anything changes, a surface this host is not served, a setting that already names somewhere else (never overwritten), live entries where the product looks while the setting is unset (they would be silently switched off), a setting or place that cannot be read (unmeasured is not unset), and a withdrawal of a setting the kit did not make. A change whose read-back is not the state asked for is refused as observed.

codes.title: a check was asked to run through a surface no taken adapter declares
codes.explanation: `check --surface <id>` runs every gate as seen from the clone that surface's product runs in, and the surface's own declaration says what that clone is: an ephemeral one names a setting outside the tree NOT MEASURED instead of failing it. A name no taken adapter declares cannot say that, so the check is refused before any gate runs, rather than silently answering the question of a check run through no surface.

codes.title: a task handed to the dispatch port is not one it will start
codes.explanation: The dispatch port is the one place a worker is started, so every refusal a dispatch can earn is taken there and not in any runtime's hook -- a gate that fires only where a runtime happens to have a pre-spawn hook is a property of the orchestrator, not a gate (ADR-017 decision 1). Refused, on pure reads, before anything is leased, made or started: what was handed over is not readable as a packet; the packet is INCOMPLETE against its declared shape; its DISPATCH-ID is routed to an adapter no enabled capability declares (a name with no referent); the id has already been dispatched on this host, or its workspace was found rather than made; or the adapter is started with a placeholder this packet states no value for, which is never filled with an empty string.

codes.title: this host declares no way to carry a dispatch out
codes.explanation: A dispatch needs two declarations the kit core never ships: an ADAPTER that says how one intelligence is started as a worker, and a PROVIDER that says how an isolated workspace is made for it. Refused rather than defaulted, in each of its forms: no dispatch adapter has been taken at all; the enabled declarations of isolation are zero or more than one (a worker with nowhere of its own would write into the host, and 'the isolated workspace' must name one place); an adapter names a placeholder or reads an artifact from a channel the port does not provide; or a declared program is not present on this machine -- what a declaration claims about somebody else's software is a claim until it is measured, and an absent program is that measurement, never a worker that quietly did nothing.

codes.title: the task vocabulary has two homes and they have parted
codes.explanation: The states a dispatched task can be in are A2A's, adopted whole, and their one home is the `task` schema. The dispatch port names the ones it writes; before the first write it holds those names against the schema's own declaration and refuses if either side has a state the other does not, rather than writing a record whose state no reader recognises. The same refusal covers a task record that does not honour its schema at any transition: a record that is not a task record is not written over the only account of what a worker did.

codes.title: what a worker's tree came back with is NOT ADMITTED
codes.explanation: A runtime the kit cannot stop mid-command is not prevented from writing; it is ISOLATED, and what it wrote is judged on RETURN (ADR-017 decision 5). Verification at return replaces prevention at write, and it only replaces it if it actually runs -- so this refusal is raised whenever the change a worker left in its leased tree either violates one of this host's declared edit gates, or cannot be read at all. Both endings are one refusal on purpose: an unjudged write is not an allowed one, and a change that could not be read admitted 'because nothing was found' would be exactly the silence that makes isolation decorative. The worker's tree, its task record and its lease are left standing: they are the only account of what was refused, and the refusal is not the moment to destroy the evidence for it. The task's OWN state is untouched by this -- whether the worker finished is one proposition and whether what it wrote may enter the host is another, and a single word doing both jobs would hide one of them.

codes.title: the corpus vocabulary cannot be read as declared
codes.explanation: Every reading of a corpus rests on a vocabulary that can be COMPARED: an order over the authority states, and exactly one of them marked as the ceiling a place gets when it declares none. This refusal is raised when that footing is missing -- two states tying at the most binding rank, or no single default ceiling -- and it is raised BEFORE any document is read, because every resolution downstream would otherwise inherit the guess and none of them would say so. A ceiling chosen by this interpreter to get past the moment would be the interpreter deciding policy (Cardinal IV), and a corpus read against an ambiguous order answers the same question differently depending on which row a reader reached first (Cardinal III). The cure is a declaration, not a fallback: the vocabulary says which state is the default and what the order is, or nothing is read at all.

codes.title: a declaration names a resolver kind nothing answers for
codes.explanation: A capability may declare that a READING reaches its pages -- a `resolves` row naming a kind and the parameters that kind needs -- and the kind is answered by whichever module owns that reading, exactly as a gate kind is answered by the module that judges it. This refusal is raised when a declaration names a kind no module publishes: almost always a spelling, occasionally a capability shipped against a kit that does not carry its resolver yet. It is refused rather than skipped because the alternative is a page that renders with a section quietly missing, which reads exactly like a corpus that had nothing to put there (Cardinal V). The set of kinds stays OPEN: a new reading is a new module publishing a row, never an edit to the interpreter that dispatches them.

codes.title: a budget is declared over a measure nothing can take
codes.explanation: A host caps a corpus-wide count by writing a budget row in its corpus map: the id of a MEASURE, the ceiling it undertakes to hold, and the date the number was taken. The measures are published by the modules of the kit that already perform those readings, and discovered exactly as gate kinds are. This refusal is raised when a row names a measure no module publishes -- almost always a spelling, occasionally a map written against a kit that does not carry that reading yet. It is refused rather than skipped because a ceiling over a count nobody can take would pass FF-CORPUS-RATCHET on every run for the rest of its life, and would read, to anyone auditing the map, exactly like a budget that was being honoured (Cardinal V). The published names are printed with the refusal: name one of them, or delete the row.

codes.title: a write is refused because what it removed could not be written down first
codes.explanation: A bounded artifact carries the current POSITION and nothing else; what was true earlier is the RECORD, and the record is append-only (ADR-020 decision 2). So every accepted write journals the TEXT it removes -- the text, not a digest of it -- BEFORE the artifact is replaced, inside the lock the writer already holds. This refusal is raised when that append could not be made durable, or when the before-image could not be written as an event of the `eviction` schema. The artifact is UNCHANGED and the removed text is still in it: a removal that cannot be written down is not performed, which is what makes deletion a move by construction rather than a discipline anybody keeps. It is refused rather than deferred because the alternative is the measured failure this mechanism exists against -- true, dated history deleted under pressure to buy room in a bounded surface, leaving no trace anywhere. Repair the journal the writer appends to (an unwritable path, a parent that is not a directory, a full disk) and write again; nothing is retried silently, because a silent retry of a write whose record failed is the same loss with one more chance to happen.

codes.title: an artifact declares a count of its own losses that is not a count
codes.explanation: A bounded artifact states, in its own front matter, how many of its removals were preserved in the record and curated nowhere -- the number a host may cap with a budget row over the measure of the same name. This refusal is raised when that field holds something other than digits. It is refused rather than read as zero: the field is the count of what this artifact has lost, and an interpreter that substituted a zero would report a corpus that has lost nothing in exactly the case where the count of its losses is unreadable (Cardinal V). Write digits, or remove the field entirely -- an artifact that says nothing has honestly said nothing, and is counted as such.

codes.title: a span was told to cool and its section declares no destination
codes.explanation: The sections of a bounded position artifact are ROWS of a declaration, and each row states the record KIND a cold span of that section belongs to (ADR-020 decision 3). Cooling is one generic passage -- evict the span, land it at the destination its section declares, journal both halves -- and it knows no section name and no path. This refusal is raised when the shape declares no such section, or declares it without a `cools_to`. Both are LEGAL states of a declaration and neither is a defect in the artifact: the first says the section has not been described yet, the second says that nothing in this section cools. What is refused is the guess. A destination invented at the moment of pressure is how true, dated history ends up filed where nobody will look for it -- tidy, preserved, and lost. Nothing was moved and the artifact is unchanged. Declare `cools_to` on the section and cool again, or remove the text through the ordinary write, where it is journalled before it leaves and counted as an unlanded removal.

codes.title: a span was carried somewhere no address came back from
codes.explanation: A landing is a reference a later reader FOLLOWS: the record kind the text went to, and the address it is now at. This refusal is raised when the port that carries a cooled span returns no usable address. It is refused rather than journalled with a blank, because an event that names a kind and no address claims the text is somewhere without saying where -- exactly as useful as a digest, and worse than useless in one way that matters: it would be counted as a MOVE, so the artifact's unlanded counter would fall while the span became unfindable. Nothing was journalled and the artifact is unchanged. Whether the carrying itself happened is the port's to report and is not assumed here in either direction; fix the port to return the address it landed at, and cool again.

codes.title: a kind of proof is claimed by two resolvers, or a reading has no word
codes.explanation: A criterion names its proof as a TYPED REFERENCE, and the kinds of reference are an open registry: a module publishes the kinds it answers and the registry finds it because it is there (ADR-020 decision 7). This refusal is raised when two modules publish the same kind -- a name that resolves to two readings is not a name, and ordering them by filename would make which reading you get a property of the alphabet -- and when a reading comes back that the status vocabulary has no word for, which happens when a row is added to the registry's answers without a row being added to the words. Note what is NOT this refusal: a reference whose kind nothing installed here answers is not an error at all. It is a reading nobody could take, it is reported as such, and it never passes and never fails. Nothing was computed and no card was touched. Publish the kind from one module, or declare the missing word where the words are declared.

codes.title: a passage a machine decides was asked for, and the reference that decides it did not hold
codes.explanation: Every passage between two work states is either a judgement a named principal holds or a computation a machine makes, and the two exclude each other (ADR-020 decision 8). This refusal is raised on the second kind: the passage was asked for, the reference the declaration names was resolved, and it did not come back true. The refusal says which of the two reasons it was, because the cure differs -- a reference that was read and did NOT hold is a fact about the work, and a reference that could not be read at all is a fact about the record, most often a referent that has moved or was never there. Neither one passes: nothing enters a computed state on an unobserved proof, and no principal may declare it instead, because a state anybody could type means only that somebody said so and turns every piece of evidence beside it into decoration. The card is unchanged and no passage was recorded. Make the reference hold, or fix what it points at.

codes.title: a unit of spend is claimed by two readings
codes.explanation: A record may declare an APPETITE -- an amount and the unit it is counted in -- and what has been spent against it is READ from the receipts this system already writes, through an open registry: a module publishes the units it can read and the registry finds it because it is there (ADR-020 decision 9). This refusal is raised when two modules publish the same unit. A name that resolves to two readings is not a name, and ordering them by filename would make which number you get a property of the alphabet. Note the two things that are NOT this refusal, because neither is an error at all. An appetite declared in a unit nothing installed here reads is a reading nobody could take: it is REPORTED, in those words, and it never passes and never fails -- a limit nothing can measure reads exactly like a limit that is being kept, which is why it is said out loud. And a limit found SPENT is not a refusal of this kind either: it is the line stopping at a door, reported with the owner named, because whether work past its limit is worth finishing is the owner's judgement and no machine's. Publish the unit from one module.

codes.title: a computation was asked for a section that has no span
codes.explanation: A section of a bounded artifact whose provenance carries the machine fact that its content is COMPUTED holds no truth of its own: it is filled from the records that own what it says, and anything a hand writes there is replaced unread (ADR-020 decision 4). This refusal is raised when there is no text the passage may address -- either the shape declares no such section as computed from anything, or the artifact does not mark out where the section stands. Both are one state and both have one cure. The place is never guessed: a computation appended wherever there happened to be room would be correct in its content and wrong in its position, which is the one kind of wrong a reader does not notice, because what it says is true. Nothing was written and the artifact is unchanged. Say which section is computed and from what, put the two marker lines the refusal prints where the section belongs, and run again. Note what is NOT this refusal: a section a principal owns is not refused here at all -- it is simply not something this passage can address, and nothing in it is ever touched.

codes.title: one computed section is marked out in two places
codes.explanation: Where a computed section stands is said by a pair of marker lines carrying its name, and the pair is what the filling passage replaces between. This refusal is raised when a name is marked out more than once in one artifact. It is refused rather than resolved by picking the first: a name that resolves to two spans is not a name, and filling both would put one fact in two places inside the very file the mechanism exists to keep single -- after which the two would drift under editing while each went on being regenerated correctly. Ordering them by position would make which span is authoritative a property of where somebody happened to paste a marker. Nothing was written and the artifact is unchanged. Remove the span that is not the section's home, and run again.

codes.title: a computed section names rows this host does not compute
codes.explanation: A computed section declares what it is one line per: a name in the view this host's own declarations already produce. This refusal is raised when that name resolves to nothing there, or to something that is not a set of rows. It is refused rather than rendered as empty, and the difference is the whole point of it -- a section that fell silent on a name nobody computes is indistinguishable from a section whose rows have all gone, so the surface would be stating an emptiness nobody declared and a reader could not tell the two apart by looking (Cardinal V). Nothing was rendered and the artifact is unchanged. Name a set this host computes, or declare the thing that would produce it.
